now_known:
MEASURED in a throwaway repo (de, 2026-09-04): the filter is only HALF the mechanism and either half alone loses the failure. (1) The error text carries neither REFUS nor FAIL -- 'error: pathspec

did not match any file(s) known to git' -- so grep -ciE 'refus|fail' over it returns 0 and a wider pattern would not have caught it. (2) THE PIPE REPLACES THE EXIT CODE: 'git commit 2>&1 | head -3' exits 0 while the same command unpiped exits 1, so even an unfiltered grep shows a green shell. (3) Nothing is staged and nothing is committed -- the failure is total, not partial. So the durable fix is shape, not vocabulary: a write runs unfiltered and its exit status is read (or set -o pipefail), because a filter over a write's output cannot tell 'nothing needed doing' from 'it failed' and a pipe additionally discards the one signal that could. 'git add && git commit' is immune: add creates the index entry, so commit sees a tracked path.
fixed_by: habit, controller side: writes run unfiltered and $? or the resulting state is read (6e, 2026-09-04). merge_main.sh stages and commits nothing, so it needs no change

The commits refute it: parent1 8444a1be has 272 rows and ZERO occurrences of the amendment, parent2 89d86882 has 273 and zero, the merge diffstat is 2 insertions and no deletions, and the file today holds 274 rows with exactly one amendment row and zero exact duplicates.
cause: MY OWN SEQUENCE, not git merge. I appended the amendment to the worktree, hit the staged-path merge refusal, and ran git restore --staged --worktree runs/experiments.jsonl to clear the index -- which silently discarded the uncommitted append. The merge then ran clean and I re-appended from a temp copy. The row-set diff I used as evidence (pre 273, post 273, one row each way) was real, but it spanned an operation I had performed three commands earlier, so it could not attribute the loss to the merge. I named a mechanism I had not traced.
fix_applied: git restore --staged --worktree on an append-only log destroys uncommitted appends with no output. Commit the append FIRST, then merge -- which is also what the staged-path refusal requires, so the two rules agree and I had the second one in front of me. Detection rule from de: check the jsonl by (name, started) key before concluding a row was lost; row 269 and row 274 both read started=2026-09-03 12:51 and only 274 carries the amendment. Separate omission found by de: EXPERIMENTS.md is rendered, not merged, and nobody ran scripts/exp.py render after the merge -- the amendment was in the jsonl and missing from the rendered file, which is what made it look lost. Rendered now, amendment present.
